subject: Item 6 and 7 Critical Hillside Overlay
comment: Members of the Commission, The proposed overlay is flawed in a number of ways. The following would be some of the biggest issues: 1. "Ridgeline" establishment seems to be redundant and then punitive to landowners who haven't developed when revealed what Provo is proposing are the ridgelines contained within the overlay. The definition within the draft ordinance talks of the highest point in between two slopes and clearly says that "a bench is not a ridgeline". The ridgelines that have been identified and proposed thus far clearly identify many existing structures in violation of the required 100 ft set back which would suggest that these ridgelines would more closely fit the definition of a "bench" seeing as how buildable areas were located within the newly proposed 100 ft set backs. Code already requires that a 30% or greater slope be left undisturbed. This requirement protects hillside sufficiently and prevents the arbitrary creation of a "ridgeline" when a case for "bench" can be made. It saves potential legal fights over terms that are difficult to define. 2. For the few land owners that would still have developable property in the affected areas, 60% of their land must remain completely undisturbed. Again this feels punitive and arbitrary. Imagine someone wants to plant fruit trees on their property for an orchard. 60% of their land, regardless of slope, can't be used?! That's clearly punitive and untenable as a standard for all land affected by the overlay. The proper role of government is to protect land owners' rights not unduly diminish them. Please do not recommend this inconsistent and arbitrary proposal.

subject: Agenda items 6 and 7
comment: Dear Planning Commisssion, Please DO NOT weaken the Hillside Overlay Zone Document! We need a document with teeth in it that will protect our foothills. Allowing changes that would favor development is NOT in the best interests of the surrounding neighborhoods or of Provo City. We need to continue to protect all of the green space we can in the foothills. Once it is altered, it can't be restored to its pristine condition. Please seriously consider what is best for future generations. Thank you! Cindy and Russ Taylor

subject: for the Planning Commission members - Critical Hillside Overlay Zone
comment: Dear Planning Commission, I live up in the Edgemont area (northeast Provo), and have been part of helping to preserve our foothills. Tonight I understand that you're going to review and possibly modify the Critical Hillside Overlay Zone paper. May I encourage you with all my heart to strengthen it if anything, and to not weaken it. We won't get a second chance to protect our foothills. This is it. Developers have no end of what they want, and they're bottom line is never for the best future good of all of Provo. Although I live in the vicinity of the foothills, they are the wonderful natural resource for everyone who lives in Provo, and beyond. Please help us to protect them. Thanks so much. Kisi Watkins Provo 801-830-6231

subject: Message to the Planning Commission Members for tonight's meeting 6/10/2020
comment: Dear Commission Members Phillips, Winden, Jensen, Howard, Jensen, Urquiaga, Anderson and Knudsen, I am writing regarding agenda item numbers 6 and 7 for tonight's meeting. I've heard that exemptions keep being made to properties that originally were included in the zone. I realize that the first version was too far reaching and the overlay group scaled it back which is good. I'm glad that changes were made so that the boundaries made more sense to properties it included. However, my understanding is that too many more exemptions are being made for whatever reasons. I think this document is good for Provo. It does not stop development nor should it. There must be a healthy balance between allowing development in Provo and protecting the green space, foothills and trails we still have. We all know once something is paved over, it's gone. Let's work together to give future generations the same access to the foothills and mountains and beautiful views that we now enjoy. Please keep this overlay document strong so that it can provide necessary guidance for sensitive areas. I hope you move this document forward with your support to the city council. Sincerely, Kaye Nelson Provo resident -- Kaye Nelson "There's no place like home."

subject: Critical Hillside Overlay Zone Document
comment: As I've looked at the progress of this document on the Provo City website and listened to comments from our neighborhood group, I see that many individuals have asked for exceptions and others are working to weaken the document by giving more and more control to developers instead of to the community. The planning commission must listen to many voices, and I don't envy you your position. However, please don't allow the voices of a few determine that the planning document is weakened to the point of being ineffective to guide development. Many people have worked long and hard in developing the plan; hopefully it will survive this round of criticism so that their work will not be wasted. Thanks again for your work for Provo City. John Bennion Associate Professor of English Brigham Young University
